text:
customer_alan: Hey — running into a 400 from the tool call endpoint when passing the request body via a heredoc in our CI. Error: "invalid character '\u00E2' in string literal". Repro below, any ideas?

support_jane: sorry you're blocked, can you paste the exact curl you used? are you using any templating or CI variables? :eyes:

customer_alan: minimal repro (weirdly only fails in our CI, works locally):

```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @- <<JSON
{
  "tool": "invoice_parser",
  "args": {
    "invoice_text": "Some text here",
  },
}
JSON
```

customer_alan: response: `{"error":"parse error: invalid character '\u00E2' at 1:2"}`

eng_ben: ok a couple things stand out: 1) trailing commas in that JSON will cause parser errors depending on the server parser 2) heredoc quoting matters — unquoted heredoc vs quoted changes how shells expand/normalize unicode and strip or preserve characters 3) CI might be injecting smart/curly quotes or doing CRLF conversions.

liz_ops: also `--data-binary @- <<JSON` vs `<<'JSON'` — with `<<JSON` the shell still performs expansions, which can introduce weird bytes if a variable contains non-ascii or if your runner interprets multiline tokens. Try `<<'JSON'` to prevent expansion.

support_jane: can you try replacing the heredoc with an explicit file to see if CI is the culprit? e.g.:

```
echo '{"tool":"invoice_parser","args":{"invoice_text":"Some text here"}}' > /tmp/payload.json
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @/tmp/payload.json
```

customer_alan: tried that — when I echo single-line to file it worked, multiline heredoc still fails in CI runner. I also tried removing trailing commas and got a different error (400 with schema mismatch for missing top-level fields) so looks like two separate problems (trailing commas + weird byte).

eng_ben: please attach the raw bytes coming from CI (base64) so we can inspect the offending char. you can do `cat payload.json | base64` and paste it.

customer_alan: here you go (base64): `eyAidG9vbCI6ICJpbnZvaWNlX3BhcnNlciIsICJhcmdzIjogeyAiaW52b2ljZV90ZXh0IjogIlNvbWUg0oAhdGV4dCBoZXJlIiB9LCAgfQ==`

liz_ops: decoding shows a 0xC2 0xA0 sequence (U+00A0 non-breaking space) between words — that often comes from copy/paste from docs or content editors. Some JSON parsers choke when unexpected non-breaking spaces are present without proper escaping.

support_jane: short-term workaround: sanitize payload in CI with `tr -d '\\u00A0'` or run `iconv -f utf8 -t utf8 -c` to drop invalid sequences before curl. Long-term: we should improve API error message to indicate byte and offset and recommend sanitization.

sre_bot: Ticket #INC-4721 created for API better-error-guidance (assigned to eng_ben).

eng_ben: follow-ups I'm going to do: 1) make parser error message include hex byte and offset 2) add a small middleware to reject JSON with trailing commas with a clear message (we already do, but tighten message) 3) add a KB entry in support docs about CI heredoc pitfalls (quoted vs unquoted heredocs, CRLF, non-breaking spaces from copy/paste).

customer_alan: thanks — workaround `<<'JSON'` + remove trailing commas fixed it in our CI. leaving this here in case others hit it. :thumbsup:

support_jane: great, closing the loop — will paste the KB link once live. :white_check_mark:
